title: K. Kamaraj: The Birth of the Midday Meal Scheme
culture_region: India / Greece / USA / South Africa / World
summary: When the finance secretary protested that there was no money in the treasury to feed millions of school children, Kamaraj roared: 'I will beg with an open bowl before the people, but no child shall study on an empty stomach!'
keywords: K. Kamaraj: The Birth of the Midday Meal Scheme
full_text:
In the early 1950s, Chief Minister K. Kamaraj was traveling by car through rural Tirunelveli.

At a railway crossing, the car halted. Kamaraj noticed several young boys herding cattle in the scorching sun.

He stepped out and called the children over:
"Little ones, why are you not in school? Why are you tending cattle?"

A young boy looked up with wide, innocent eyes:
"Sir, if I go to school, who will feed me? If I graze cattle, the farmer gives me a bowl of porridge!"

The words pierced Kamaraj's heart like an arrow. He sat in his car in heavy silence, tears welling in his eyes.

Upon reaching the Secretariat in Madras, Kamaraj summoned education and finance bureaucrats:
"Starting immediately, the government will provide a free hot meal every day to every poor child attending primary school in Tamil Nadu!"

The finance secretary panicked:
"Chief Minister, this is impossible! The state exchequer has zero funds for this! Feeding millions of children every day will bankrupt the treasury! The law does not permit it!"

Kamaraj hitched up his khadi dhoti and struck the desk:
"Do not lecture me on financial rules!
Opening schools is useless if a child sits faint with hunger! How can a starving brain absorb lessons?
If the treasury has no money, I will take my shawl and beg door-to-door before the people of Tamil Nadu to feed my children!
Change the rules! No child in this state shall be denied schooling because of hunger!"

The bureaucracy bowed before his moral fire. In 1956, the historic **Midday Meal Scheme** was launched across Tamil Nadu.

School enrollments skyrocketed by millions. The United Nations lauded it as a global model. Kamaraj proved that genuine statesmanship is born from empathy for the poorest child.
moral: Social welfare is not charity; nourishing the vulnerable is the primary obligation of a humane civilization.
